The implementation is in [output_model_new.py](/root/lumen-clean/lumen-sosp26-ae-origin/runs/kernelbench_generation_level1_moonbridge/p99/round0/output_model_new.py) with two AveLang kernels:

**`triplet_reduce_kernel`** — one block per sample (32768 blocks of 256 threads each). Each thread serially accumulates squared differences over 32 feature elements (8192 / 256), then all 256 threads perform a shared-memory tree reduction to produce per-sample squared L2 distances `d_ap_sq` and `d_an_sq` in f32.

**`triplet_loss_kernel`** — a single block reduces across the batch. Each thread reads per-sample squared distances, computes `al.sqrt` for the true L2 norm, applies the triplet loss formula `max(d_ap - d_an + margin, 0)`, and tree-reduces to a scalar mean.

**Results:** compiled on gfx942 (MI300X), passed 5/5 correctness trials, 1.98ms mean runtime vs 7.62ms reference — roughly 3.8x faster.

The key fix along the way was using L2 distance (with `al.sqrt`) rather than squared L2, matching PyTorch's `TripletMarginLoss(p=2)` semantics. The `al.f32` scalar kernel parameter also tripped up the AMDGPU launcher, so I routed the margin through a module-level variable captured at kernel compile time, following the same pattern as the fused linear ReLU example.
